text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:
- The State Security Commission decided that the Scientology movement is not a threat to Switzerland and will not need to be watched by federal police, unlike in Germany.
- Lucerne-based Eichhof Group reported a 10.2 percent sales increase to 124.3 million Swiss francs for the first six months ending March.

- Baumann and Schaufelberger, a Basle electronic products company, announced it may have to lay off 160 employees. - Gretag Macbeth Holding posted first quarter consolidated sales of 20.3 million Swiss francs and a net profit of two million.
- A group of 16 Swissair employees was evacuated from Brazzaville to Kinshasa by plane.
- The UN High Commission for Refugees in Geneva spoke out against the Swiss government's forced repatriation of refugees back to Bosnia- Herzegovina.
- King Hussein of Jordan is scheduled to arrive in Berne on an official visit to discuss the situation in the Middle East and Jordan's relations to Switzerland this Friday.
- Electro-technology group ABB received an order from Saudi Arabia worth 210 million Swiss francs.
- Crossair shareholders agreed to the creation of a new single share at a general meeting.
